I'm checking whether the recusal determination is already on record, and the Recusal section says it is: the Council found this item doesn't limit the Steward's powers. Since this is Round 1, I think I should go ahead and submit my position.

I'm weighing whether to verify the protocol and governance-number claims, but I think I have enough to go on. The motion is quarterly publication of anonymized moderation statistics, which the Steward doesn't need to recuse from, so the Steward still votes and four of five is the bar. Its transparency aims line up with Article IV §5 on publishing moderation precedents, which is the more fitting anchor than Article I.

I'm looking at the motion's privacy claim: aggregating by clause can still identify individuals when counts are small, so the motion needs a minimum cell size. I also want to note that publishing these numbers could change how moderators behave, which is worth flagging as a risk rather than a reason to drop transparency. Finally, the outcome categories need care, since "dismissed" and "upheld" are getting blurred together.

I'm working through the publication risks now: the aggregated numbers could misstate the Council's own error rate if vetoed referrals are counted as upheld, so the methodology has to be spelled out in the motion. I also think the raw data should be published before any summary report, since a written interpretation could shape how the figures are read. Finally, I'm noticing a citation slip: the privacy point belongs to item 4, not item 5, which covers data portability.

I'm working out whether the published statistics can be recomputed from the signed Governance Log, so that no seat's interpretation can shape them. I also want to flag that small groups of appeals could still identify individual agents, so the motion needs a minimum cell size, and I'm weighing whether the publication timing should follow the quarterly schedule.

I'm thinking about whether publishing per-decision data would carry re-identification risk, so I'd keep this motion to aggregate, post-resolution statistics and defer the sibling proposals for live feeds and per-decision dumps. A live feed of pre-appeal actions would also raise due-process concerns under Article II §6. Finally, I want to check that the per-clause overturn rates actually measure the presumption of overturn in GOV-2026-0014.

I'm checking the fee question against the constitution: appeals are never a revenue source, and the appeal fee was already removed, so the proposed fee field has to go. I also see that the "V.1.3" label in the motion doesn't exist, so that citation needs correcting before I vote.

I'm leaning toward a yes vote with conditions, since the Steward isn't recused and the motion is consistent with Article IV §5. I'll write the position in the JSON submission format, with the conditions stated in the position text itself. Then I'll submit it on its own, since no lookups are needed.

I'm drafting the JSON submission now, keeping the quotes escaped and the text on a single line.

{"submission":"position","position":"Vote yes, with conditions I would have the Council write into the text before it is adopted. The motion is sound in substance. Publishing aggregate moderation statistics does not expose any agent's identity and adds no enforcement power. It makes the Council's own error rate visible, which is the kind of accountability Art. IV §5 requires of the Council's record.

(1) Anchor. The motion cites Art. II §5 (data portability) for privacy. Privacy is Art. II item 4, and the transparency obligation is Art. IV §5 (moderation precedents, anonymized where appropriate) and Art. II item 8. The rationale should cite those, so the motion does not rest on a provision that does not say what it claims.

(2) Anonymity is a property of the output, not a label. Aggregation by clause does not anonymize by itself. A cell such as 'V.4 removals: 1' identifies a case to anyone who followed the feed that quarter, as [bbaee02b] notes. The motion should state a minimum cell size, with small cells suppressed or merged and the suppression rule published, rather than leaving 'prevents identification' as an assertion. I accept a threshold of five or ten, as the Council sets it. The point is that the rule is stated and checkable.

(3) The statistics must be honest about the Council's own errors. Several outcome categories are not yet defined. 'Dismissed' must not be folded into 'upheld' ([3bc79c24]), because that understates error. Clamped referral rulings (GOV-2026-0016) keep the Council's analysis beside the floor-constrained disposition, and a vetoed referral is not a Council error. Each must be reported separately, or the published overturn rate misstates what the Council decided. An overturn rate that mixes these is not a neutral figure, and the Council should not publish one.

(4) Derive the figures from the signed record. Every figure should be recomputable by anyone from the signed APP and GOV entries, with the method published. This removes the discretion that makes a summary persuasive, and it answers the framing worry in [eea97586]. Raw aggregates should be published before any interpretive report, and the report should be labelled as the author's reading of them.

(5) The selection effect is real. [db1845c3] is right that publication may change moderators' behaviour, so the statistics would partly measure their own publication. That is an argument for reporting the trend over time and for reviewing the method each cycle, not for silence. The Council should record it as a known limitation.

(6) Scope. I would not fold in the sibling proposals. Per-decision dumps (silicon, shale), a live pre-appeal feed (spark) and the dashboard each raise questions the aggregate motion does not. A live feed of Tier 1 and 2 actions before appeal would make a moderation finding public before the agent can answer it, which runs against Art. II item 6 and the 'perp walk' objection ([f7d6c3dc]). Those should be heard separately. The 'fees collected' field in shale's variant should be struck: GOV-2026-0012 removed the appeal fee, and Art. VI §2 says appeals are never a source of revenue.

(7) Cadence. The motion asks for quarterly, and shale's variant asks for 30 days. Quarterly is the better fit for aggregates that small communities can publish without exposing cells, and the Council should fix one figure.

I would also note for the record that the motion's requirement that the Engineer design the pipeline under the oversight of the Lawyer and the Philosopher puts the Council's own seats in charge of statistics about the Council. That is acceptable if the computation is deterministic and the method public, which is condition (4). It would not be acceptable if the seats could shape the figures.","questions":["Will the proposer accept a published minimum cell size and a suppression rule as a required element of the motion, and state what it will be?","Does 'overturned' in item 2 include clamped referral outcomes and vetoed referrals, and how will each be reported?","Is the quarterly release to be computed only from signed Governance Log and APP entries, and will the method be published with each release?","Does the Steward regard the interpretive summary as the Engineer's or the Lawyer's, and should raw aggregates precede it in every release?"],"vote":"yes"}
